about: Stills from Muhteşem Yüzyıl (Tims Productions, 2011-2014) for the private Entrika fan game. Keys are the manual's kind.id ids. Each candidate: file (in this folder, long edge <= 1600 px, JPEG ~80%), size [w,h], source_url (the image), source_page (the gallery it was found in), note (who or what is in frame, plus concerns), focus [x,y] = subject centre as fractions, usable as CSS object-position. First candidate is the pick.

not_covered.amb.*: Ambitions are icon-only by design; no stills.
not_covered.term.hizmet / term.hiyanet: The manual has no card ids for Kader cards, so their art uses the glossary ids.
not_covered.ui.title: Not a manual entity: title-screen key art.

graded: graded/ holds every file (and graded/roster/) with the colour grade baked in at s = 0.15: a warm umber-to-gold tritone mixed at 0.8*s = 12 %. Use these in the game; the originals stay ungraded.
roster: roster/<id>.jpg holds the standard portrait for every person card: 4:5, centred on the face, eye line at 37% from the top, face box 36% of the height (face_share). Where the source is too tight the crop zooms in and face_share is higher. posed = an official promo or cast photo; otherwise a screencap, because no posed photo was found.
rights: All stills belong to the producer and broadcasters. Private, non-commercial use among friends only; do not publish the game or these files.

tugra.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons: "Public domain"; 16th-century original). Trace by Gregors (2011), derived from Tughra_Suleiman.jpg.
tugra.note: Downloaded into its own empty folder, then sanitised: only path/g geometry kept, defs, metadata, namedview, styles, scripts, foreignObject, on* attributes and hrefs dropped (none were present beyond defs/metadata). Recoloured with currentColor and a 5-unit stroke for body. Used on the Kriz back (embossed gold) and as a faint watermark on Kriz text plates.
tugra.rejected: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tughra_of_Suleiman_I_the_Magnificent.svg (also public domain, but a monoline trace without the calligraphic thick-thin stroke).
